title.value: Rocket Lab (RKLB) Stock Could Be A Bargain Despite Its Big Run

source_messages.body_text:
Rocket Lab has ridden a powerful three year run in its share price, while also pushing ahead with big moves in launch, satellites and now communications. That kind of shift in scale leaves a clear question for investors who own or follow Rocket Lab stock: Is today's valuation really grounded in the cash the business can generate over time?

Over the past three years the share price has delivered a very large gain of about 1,600%, which puts real pressure on whether the current market value is fully supported by the company's underlying cash flows.

The recently completed US$1.94b equity raise to fund the Iridium acquisition removes the need for a large bridge loan and may support more predictable cash generation, but it also increases the share count that those future cash flows have to cover.

If you'd rather focus on book value, this one's for you. See why Rocket Lab's 12.3x P/B tells a different valuation story.

The issue now is whether Rocket Lab's current share price around US$71.98 is adequately explained by its cash flows when viewed through a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) lens.

If you are weighing Rocket Lab against other potential opportunities on this theme, it can help to compare it with 29 high quality undervalued stocks that also screen well on quality.

Does Rocket Lab Look Undervalued on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here focuses on the cash Rocket Lab can return to shareholders over time rather than short term earnings. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at a loss of about $370.5 million, so the starting point in the calculation is still deeply negative even before any growth is layered in.

Analysts feeding into this DCF expect free cash flow to move from losses toward positive territory, with projections that reach into the hundreds of millions of dollars and then several billions in later years. That path assumes Rocket Lab converts its launch track record and the planned Iridium acquisition into much stronger cash generation. The recent US$1.94b equity raise cuts financing risk for that deal, but the higher share count means any future free cash flow is now spread more thinly across each share at a trading price of US$71.98. Find out what Rocket Lab could be worth using our Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) estimate.

The Rocket Lab Narrative: What Would Justify Today's Price?

Narratives pick up where the Rocket Lab valuation puzzle leaves off by spelling out which paths for growth, margins and earnings would need to hold for the stock to be worth materially more or less than today's price. Each scenario ties a specific fair value to a clear storyline about Rocket Lab's potential catalysts and key risks, so you can track over time which version of events appears closest to reality on Simply Wall St's Community page.

Rocket Lab has sparked sharply different views on Simply Wall St, with the community split between a big upside story and a stretched valuation.

Bull case: 26% undervalued

"Rocket Lab USA seeks to vertically integrate itself throughout the $800 billion space 'backbone' in order to attract the customers operating within that $1 trillion top component of the 'space economy'…"

Discover why this Narrative puts Rocket Lab at 26% undervalued.

Bear case: 343% overvalued

"The entire valuation is 'priced for perfection,' which means any delay causes volatility…"

Explore why this Narrative puts Rocket Lab at 343% overvalued.

One more Rocket Lab check that belongs beside the valuation work

Price, cash flows and storylines give you part of Rocket Lab, but the recent trading activity by people inside the business can reveal a very different signal. See the recent insider selling flagged for Rocket Lab.

title.value: Press Release: Rocket Lab Secures Largest-Ever Electron Commercial Deal: 20-Launch Contract for Synspective

source_messages.body_text: LONG BEACH, Calif., Sept. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB) ("Rocket Lab" or the "Company"), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today announced it has signed a multi-year launch agreement for 20 new Electron missions with Tokyo-based Earth observation company Synspective. The contract is the largest commercial launch contract for Electron in Rocket Lab's history and brings the total number of Electron missions for Synspective to 47 -- the most of any Rocket Lab launch customer. The remaining terms of the deal are undisclosed. Rocket Lab will launch 20 StriX synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites to sun-synchronous orbit (SSO) from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1. The missions are scheduled to take place annually from 2028 through 2031, accelerating Synspective's goal to build a comprehensive satellite constellation capable of imaging any location on Earth within hours, day or night, and through any weather conditions. Sir Peter Beck, Rocket Lab founder and CEO, says: "When constellation builders want control over their destiny, they come to Rocket Lab. Synspective was one of Electron's earliest customers and together we have proven that tailored, dedicated launch is the fastest and most reliable path to scaling small satellite constellations. Signing twenty launches in a single deal is a massive vote of confidence not just in Electron, but in the launch cadence, mission reliability, and orbital precision that Rocket Lab consistently delivers." Dr. Motoyuki Arai, Synspective founder and CEO, says: "Electron's precision and reliability have played a central role in steadily scaling our StriX constellation. Through this process, our partnership has grown into something built not only on technical progress but on a deep, team-level trust between us. On behalf of Synspective, I would like to once again express our gratitude for the quality of service, the flexibility, and the truly excellent team behind it. Securing another 20 dedicated launches now gives us long-term certainty for our constellation expansion - a powerful booster toward building the infrastructure needed for a resilient future. We look forward to continuing this journey together." Today's launch agreement is the latest in a wave of multi-launch contracts awarded to Rocket Lab this year, pushing the Company's launch backlog beyond 100 missions. At a time when global launch capacity is bottlenecked and constellation operators face mounting pressure on tight timelines to deploy and replenish their constellations, Rocket Lab stands apart as the proven alternative delivering unmatched reliability and rapid operational cadence. Rocket Lab Media Murielle Baker media@rocketlabusa.com About Rocket Lab Rocket Lab (Nasdaq: RKLB) is an end-to-end space company delivering rockets, satellites, and spacecraft components for commercial, government, and defense missions. Driven by its industry-leading small-lift rockets Electron and HASTE and its upcoming reusable Neutron medium-lift rocket, Rocket Lab delivers reliable and responsive launch for the world's most important missions from constellation deployment to missile defense. Rocket Lab's satellites and components have powered more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit, as well as deep-space exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Learn more at www.rocketlabcorp.com. title.value: Rocket Lab Stock Rises on Record Electron Launch Deal and Citi Buy Rating -- Barrons.com

source_messages.body_text: By Mariapaula Gonzalez and Al Root Rocket Lab has launched small satellites for years, gradually emerging as a potential competitor to SpaceX. Now, Rocket Lab just scored its largest commercial launch contract in its history, signaling strong demand for small-satellite constellation deployments. Rocket Lab secured a multiyear deal with Tokyo-based Synspective for 20 new Electron launches to deploy the company's radar satellites, the company announced Wednesday. The agreement marks the largest commercial launch contract in Rocket Lab's history, as well as the most missions ordered by a single customer. Specific financial terms of the deal were undisclosed. The agreement brings Synspective's total contracted Electron launches to 47, the most of any Rocket Lab customer. Shares of Rocket Lab rose 1.3% in midday trading to $70.56, while the S&P 500 was down 0.2%. Also helping was a new bullish rating from Citi. Analyst John Godyn called Rocket Lab stock a "core holding" in a new report. He sees Rocket Lab as an industry leader and started with a $105 price target for shares. Overall, Rocket Lab is popular on Wall Street, with 83% of analysts covering the company rating shares Buy, according to FactSet. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%. The average analyst price target for Rocket Lab stock is about $112. Rocket Lab will launch 20 radar satellites for Synspective to expand a satellite network designed to image any location on Earth within hours, day or night and in any weather. The missions are expected to take place over four years, with launches scheduled annually from 2028 to 2031. Rocket Lab said the agreement pushes its total launch backlog past 100 missions. It comes at a time when the space sector has faced a global rocket shortage and growing launch delays. Thursday's gains left Rocket Lab stock up 1% year to date. Up just 1% in 2026, however, belies the path shares took. Rocket Lab stock traded as high as $151 in May, just ahead of the trillion-dollar SpaceX IPO. SpaceX essentially created the modern space economy, and investors bid up many space-related shares in anticipation of the record-setting IPO. Then, Rocket Lab shares traded below $60 in July as SpaceX shares, and other space stocks, slid after some of the initial euphoria wore off. Through the volatility, Rocket Lab has continued to perform well. The company reported better-than-expected second-quarter sales in August and offered above-Street guidance for the third quarter. The space business is booming as the cost to reach orbit has fallen.
